newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish bankers say rate rise not needed - survey.
newsitem.headline: Polish bankers say rate rise not needed - survey.

text.p: Most Polish bankers believe an official interest rate rise in the near future would be unjustified, according to a survey by the independent Institute for Opinion and Market Research Pentor.
Pentor said 89 percent of 210 bank managers polled felt an interest rate increase was not necessary while 14 percent said that it was. One percent had no opinion.
The National Bank of Poland has been signalling that it might have to raise nominal rates, currently at 22 and 25 percent, soon to curb booming credit for households and companies.
In 1996, household credit jumped 108.5 percent and company credit rose 35.4 percent.
